item.problem_title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
item.problem_statement: An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act, when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins, and it has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as scheduled visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation handle the misalignment; neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring applies; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. Selection tools exist and use outcome information: cross-validated variance has been evaluated as a measure of data support for choosing a discretization. item.evidence: For one class of question, when to add a second agent, this identifies the specific design choices that manufacture immortal time, distinguishes the two mechanisms, selection and strategy misclassification, and demonstrates an emulation that avoids both while reporting what the biased choices would have given. item.paper: Bariatric metabolic surgery and cancer risk: Target trial emulation using iterative time distribution matching.
item.evidence: Time zero for the unexposed is assigned by an explicit, iterated procedure that matches the distribution of pre-exposure time rather than by a landmark or an arbitrary index date, and the paper reports what the conventional approach would have given in the same data, 0.70 against 0.49. It also names the three quantities that determine how much distortion remains. The procedure aligns a distribution rather than establishing when eligibility, assignment and follow-up coincide for each person, and it is specific to a one-time surgical exposure.

verdicts.reason: Public synthetic data, released analysis code, a base cohort, and weight-performance code materially improve operational auditability for this example. The tutorial does not solve missing versioned phenotype logic or protocol decision logs across substantive emulations, so partial addressing is appropriate.

item.problem_title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
item.problem_statement: The TARGET statement asks for the target protocol, its data mapping, the estimands, the assumptions, the estimates and the sensitivity analyses, and is a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias certification. An emulation is not externally auditable when its final analysis code, its complete versioned phenotype logic and its weight diagnostics are unavailable, and in current practice they are: most emulations are irreproducible in operative detail despite faithful protocol reporting. Where the real data cannot be shared, code plus a documented schema, a container and synthetic fixtures establishes that the pipeline executes and what it does; it does not reproduce the published estimate, and auditability rather than reproduction is what such a release can deliver. Material protocol amendments belong in a versioned decision log, which nothing currently requires.
item.paper: Demystifying Clone-Censor-Weighting to Studying Treatment Initiation Windows: An Example Using Publicly Available Synthetic Medicare Claims Data.
item.evidence: The whole analysis is reproducible by a reader: the data are Medicare synthetic public use files, the SAS code is in the article appendix and on GitHub, and the base analytic cohort is published with it, including code for examining censoring weight performance and for visualizing the exposure distributions. That is the artifact set the entry says emulations do not release, supplied for a tutorial rather than for a substantive study.
item.quote: SAS code is included in the appendix of this article, along with the base analytic cohort, are on GitHub at https://github.com/mawcpharmdphd/CCW_tutorial .

item.problem_title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
item.problem_statement: A correctly implemented emulation prevents specific design-induced temporal biases and does not create exchangeability. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurement all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing it. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, identify under distinct and partly untestable assumptions and sometimes target different estimands. They therefore cannot be mechanically ordered or combined: doing so requires an explicit joint model aligned to one estimand, and no such model is in use, so there is no convention for reporting what each tool contributed or for reconciling them when they disagree. item.paper: Effectiveness of a Covid mRNA Vaccine Against Two Early Variants: A Reanalysis of Published Data.
item.evidence: A negative control outcome, non-Covid death, is used not as a qualitative signal that residual confounding exists but to derive a bias factor that is then applied to the estimate, which changes the conclusion. That is the integration the entry says is missing, carried out on one dataset with a correction the paper itself calls rudimentary and with no procedure specifying when a given negative control licenses a given correction.

verdicts.reason: The quotation supports an unusually informative narrative comparison rather than a binary replication label. It does not provide a paired estimand-aligned contrast with joint uncertainty, so it does not deliver the calibrated comparison procedure the problem identifies as missing.

item.problem_title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
item.problem_statement: Agreement between an emulation and a trial is informative only when the estimands, populations and measurements are close enough to be comparable, and better design alignment is empirically associated with stronger concordance. The benchmarking programs report this in graded form. What is cited downstream is a binary label, usually derived from interval overlap or direction agreement, and that label discards magnitude and uncertainty and cannot diagnose why two estimates differ: two studies estimating the same quantity imprecisely agree by that criterion, and two estimating different quantities precisely disagree. No reported measure, graded or binary, separates estimand mismatch from random error, because doing so requires aligning the estimands first and then reporting a paired contrast with joint uncertainty, which no benchmarking report currently does as a matter of course.
item.paper: Emulating the EPIC trial using VetCompass primary-care data: causal effects of pimobendan in UK dogs with grade IV/VI heart murmurs.
item.evidence: The comparison is not reported as replicated or not. Each source of divergence is named and its direction argued: an intention-to-treat estimand against the trial's per-protocol, an explicitly modeled competing event the trial did not model, different case definitions and populations, and a different time zero, with the emulation's more conservative estimate attributed to the first two. The agreement is then stated separately for each outcome, close for survival and diverging in the untreated arm for heart failure. That is the calibrated comparison the entry asks for, done once rather than established as a convention.
item.quote: The current study evaluated an intention to treat estimate, rather than the per-protocol estimate measured in the EPIC trial, and accounted for the competing event of death, potentially explaining the more conservative estimate for the treatment effect in the current study.

item.evidence: Death is treated as a competing event with its own cumulative incidence rather than as censoring, and the consequence is reported and interpreted: treatment raised the 5-year probability of dying without heart failure, which follows mechanically from fewer treated dogs reaching heart failure first. Handling the competing event as part of the estimand rather than as cleaning is what makes that reading available.

verdicts.reason: A question-specific ROBINS-E-derived checklist is not an assumption dashboard. The evidence explicitly combines untestable treatment-allocation assumptions with more diagnosable items without labeling their different evidentiary status, which reproduces the problem's central deficiency.

item.problem_title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
item.problem_statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from observed data. Neither, strictly, can positivity, model correctness or phenotype validity: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them. Current reports blur both distinctions. A propensity-score overlap plot is offered and the reader infers that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot is a partial diagnostic of one of them and silent on the rest. No standard panel exists, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and an absent diagnostic cannot be distinguished from one that was run and not reported. A single panel cannot be adequate for every design, which is a constraint on the solution rather than an argument against it.
item.paper: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Receptor Agonists and Cancer Prevention: Methodological Pitfalls in Observational Studies.
item.evidence: Seven criteria are named for one question, and a published study is scored against each, which produces something closer to an assumption inventory than a narrative limitations paragraph. Two of the seven are the untestable ones, adjustment for body fatness and treatment allocation, and they are scored alongside the checkable ones without distinguishing what evidence could move each. The instrument is also question-specific and derived by hand from ROBINS-E.
item.quote: We modified the ROBINS-E framework for assessing risk of bias, identifying seven methodological criteria specific to this research question, against which data should be interpreted.
